scripts.//vercel-build: Vercel runs this in preference to `build`. The Prisma client is generated into node_modules and node_modules is not in the repo, so without this step the deploy compiles against a client that was never written. It has to be spelled out here rather than in a root postinstall: the generated client is a build artifact of this app, and a postinstall would also fire on every local `npm install` and in CI, which already generates it explicitly.
scripts.//build:local: Vercel injects env from the dashboard, so `build` must stay bare. Locally the same env lives in the repo-root .env, which Next does not look for from apps/web. SKIP_ENV_VALIDATION because `next build` sets NODE_ENV=production, which trips the production-only rules against a development .env — this build checks the bundle, not the secrets.
scripts.//start:local: Serves what `build:local` produced, with the repo-root env `start` does not look for. This is the only way to exercise the PWA from a phone: `offline/register.tsx` skips registration unless NODE_ENV is production, so under `dev` there is no service worker, no precached shell and nothing to install.
